notes: The usage-based coefficients are taken from the Cloud Carbon Footprint (CCF) methodology and its AWS constants file (cloud-carbon-footprint/packages/aws/src/domain/AwsFootprintEstimationConstants.ts, trunk, read 2026-10-10; methodology page https://www.cloudcarbonfootprint.org/docs/methodology/, Apache-2.0). Derivations: vcpu_hours = (MIN_WATTS_AVG 0.74 W + 50% default utilisation x (MAX_WATTS_AVG 3.5 W - 0.74 W)) = 2.12 W = 0.00212 kWh per vCPU-hour; memory_gb_hours = MEMORY_COEFFICIENT 0.000392 kWh per GB-hour; storage_gb_months = HDDCOEFFICIENT 0.65 Wh per TB-hour = 0.00000065 kWh per GB-hour x 730 h = 0.0004745 kWh per GB-month (SSD, 1.2 Wh per TB-hour, would be 0.000876); PUE = PUE_AVG 1.135. The cost_based factors have no CCF counterpart: they are the platform authors' rough fallbacks for sources that expose cost only, and are not sourced. Embodied emissions are not included: CCF derives them per instance type from Teads data, which this set does not import. A change of any number is a NEW version, never an edit of this file.
caveats: Embodied emissions (the M term of SCI) are not included: figures are operational emissions only.
Usage-based coefficients follow the published CCF constants for AWS averages (50% default CPU utilisation, average vCPU power, HDD storage); other clouds and instance types use the same averages.
Rows marked cost_based are rough estimates derived from spend with factors chosen by the platform authors; they are not sourced and have low confidence.
